decisions.reason: The candidate's same-message INTRODUCE already records the four policy destinations and their footer-menu access point; no additional or corrected Event is needed.
The client says the Sign In and Account Provisioning pages may have the outlined footer, but 'perhaps' does not establish that the expanded footer is required on the Cognito Sign-In page.
The informational pages are said to need a background and header logo, while inclusion of the outlined footer is only tentative ('perhaps'), so propagation to the required page shell is not safe.
Adding and specifying footer links does not change the established requirement that the landing-page header menu remains disabled.
The possible solid brand-color treatment is specific and tentative footer styling; it does not change the shared dark page theme.
The footer content specification does not change the landing page's selected concepts, colors, typography, buttons, or unresolved logo treatment.
The shared footer content does not alter the landing page's section order, How It Works sequence, or copy plan.
The source specifies the website footer, not the distinct footer component within the admin workspace shell.
The tentative suggestion to use a brand color for the footer does not modify the required token-sheet fields or provide a new token value.
The footer's content and layout blocks do not change the reusable responsive rules or breakpoint basis.
The footer specification does not change the plain HTML and Tailwind CSS build stack.
The footer update does not affect the hero text-emphasis requirement.
